sources.supports: Supports the Québec phrase maïs en grains for kernel corn; read with the separate maïs sucré entry, which says sweet corn is sold in kernels. It does not name dried sweet corn.

sources.title: Health Canada, Canadian Nutrient File food code 2068: Corn, sweet, yellow, on or off the cob, boiled, drained / Maïs sucré, jaune, avec ou sans épi, bouilli, égoutté
sources.locator: Food code 2068; official item description and available serving sizes.
sources.supports: One cooked and drained sweet-corn entry includes on-cob and off-cob presentations. Its volume conversions, ear weights, and refuse percentage are specific to that item and do not define a generic corn measure.

sources.title: Health Canada, Chaudrée de palourdes crémeuse
sources.locator: Ingredient list and recipe tips.
sources.supports: Calls for 250 mL (1 cup) of maïs en grains and allows fresh or frozen corn; this is a recipe-specific kernel request, not a general measure or mapping.

decisions.reason: Present in the legacy RecipeKeeper catalog but absent from the canonical bundled seed; reconcile identity and aliases before acceptance.

Reject a standalone generic corn / maïs ingredient identity and any automatic mapping to corn kernels. The OQLF entry uses maïs / corn for both plant and grain; the distinct maïs en grains entry names kernels, while bundled recipes require corn only where its state is explicit, such as ears, frozen kernels, or syrup. Health Canada's CNF code 2068 spans cooked sweet corn with or without the cob, not generic raw corn. No source supports a single recipe-ready meaning for bare corn.

sources.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, Specific nutrient content claim requirements

decisions.reason: Removed source-less draft density and unit-mapping values from the active bundled catalog. Restore a value only with source, exact food/form, unit convention, method or basis, and reviewer disposition.

Verified cornstarch / fécule de maïs as the extracted starch identity. OQLF lists the same English phrase corn flour for Québec ground-maize flour and as a UK term for cornstarch. Because catalog aliases have no region scope, removed the global corn flour alias from cornstarch; retain the explicit names cornstarch / fécule de maïs and whole-kernel corn flour / farine de maïs. Keep the unqualified English phrase unresolved.

Add the OQLF-listed English spelling corn starch and French preferred term amidon de maïs as aliases of the existing cornstarch / fécule de maïs identity. Keep both canonical displays and leave the unqualified corn flour collision unresolved.

Record only a one-way cornstarch-to-tapioca-starch candidate for liquid thickening. Iowa State Extension reports 2 tablespoons tapioca starch per 1 tablespoon cornstarch and attributes that ratio to Bob's Red Mill, while Bob's Red Mill's direct All About Starches guide gives 4 tablespoons tapioca starch per 3 tablespoons cornstarch. Keep the conflicting volume amounts unresolved; do not select, average, reconcile, reverse, or activate either amount. Keep Iowa State's separate 1:1 instant-tapioca statement out of the extracted-starch finding because it names a different form.

Record the five published cornstarch portions as source-specific observations only. The CNF Food Code and two baking charts use different quantity bases, the chart quarter-cup values conflict (28 g versus 32 g), and the chart cup capacities and row methods are not specified. Keep measurementState blocked_pending_evidence; do not derive density, unit mappings, a generic measure, conversion, or substitution.

substitutionFindings.context: Sauce or gravy thickening, including cheese sauce; apply only where the ingredient role is thickener and the recipe method uses the source-supported context.
substitutionFindings.basis: 1 Tbsp cornstarch per 1 cup liquid versus 2 Tbsp all-purpose flour per 1 cup liquid. Source compares quantities at a fixed liquid amount; this is not a general free-standing mass or volume ratio.
expectedEffects: Flour-thickened sauce is cloudy and opaque; cornstarch-thickened sauce is transparent and glossy.
limitations: Flour works best in sauces prepared with fat, such as a roux.
The active resolver cannot enforce thickener role or cooking method and has no quantity-unit basis; do not activate as an automatic rule.

substitutionFindings.context: A liquid-thickening context where cornstarch serves as the thickener. The reviewed sources do not name a specific recipe, sauce, or other liquid preparation.
substitutionFindings.basis: The amount is unresolved: Iowa State Extension reports 2 tablespoons tapioca starch per 1 tablespoon cornstarch and attributes that recommendation to Bob's Red Mill. Bob's Red Mill's direct All About Starches guide gives 4 tablespoons tapioca starch per 3 tablespoons cornstarch. Both are volume ratios; the sources do not reconcile them.
expectedEffects: Bob's Red Mill describes tapioca starch as adding a shiny gloss to sauces and cornstarch as adding an opaque quality.
limitations: Do not select, average, reconcile, or activate either conflicting volume ratio pending evidence that resolves the difference.

Iowa State Extension separately gives a 1:1 cornstarch-to-instant-tapioca statement; keep it out of this extracted-starch finding. The source distinguishes instant/minute tapioca, pearls, flakes, and powders and says the forms are not interchangeable.
Keep this candidate limited to starch thickening; do not extend it to gluten-free baking, binding, coatings, or other ingredient roles.
Do not create an automatic substitution rule or recipe-line link. The candidate amount remains unresolved, and the runtime cannot enforce thickener role or the source volume basis.

decisions.reason: Hold pending recipe demand. Keep freshwater crayfish/crawfish distinct from langouste, despite colloquial English overlap noted by OQLF.

Retain only freshwater-qualified singular aliases; do not add crawfish/crawdads because the English terms also overlap with langouste in Québec usage. Species, shelling, cooking, and preservation states remain unresolved. Add no forms, measures, density, mappings, conversions, yields, recipe links, or substitutions.

Record lemon juice and generic vinegar as separate, source-bounded alternatives for stabilizing whipped egg whites when cream of tartar is unavailable. Preserve the per-egg-white quantity range and flavor limitation; do not create a general substitute or active runtime rule.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only creamy buckwheat hot cereal / céréales chaudes crémeuses au sarrasin for the plain single-grain packaged cereal product. The current Canadian French manufacturer list attests the grammatical French product wording; OQLF supports sarrasin as the base food name, not the compound. Keep it separate from buckwheat flour, flakes, puffed buckwheat, roasted dry groats, mixed-grain cereals, and prepared kasha. Keep aliases empty to preserve the hot-cereal qualifier. Product-specific serving/package values are not generalized. Add no forms, measures, density, unit mappings, conversions, yields, recipe links, or substitutions.

sources.title: Government of Québec, Wild and domestic mushrooms
sources.locator: Section on domestic cultivated mushrooms naming white, cremini, and portobello under Agaricus bisporus.
sources.supports: Supports current Canadian English market wording for white, cremini, and portobello mushrooms within Agaricus bisporus; food-safety page, not a formal identity standard.

sources.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, D-94-26 mushroom and vegetable import list

sources.supports: Supports a white-button versus brown-Agaricus market distinction and names crimini/portabella under brown categories. Survey groupings are for reporting and are not a synonym policy.

No maturity conversion, forms, measurements, recipe links, or substitutions are established.

sources.title: OQLF Grand dictionnaire terminologique, cretons

sources.title: Dictionary of Canadianisms on Historical Principles, cretons

sources.supports: Canadian English lexicography marks cretons as a Quebec French borrowing and defines the food as a pork-and-onion spread cooked in pork fat and seasoned with spices. This supports the English display, not a universal formula.

sources.locator: Product name, description, product category, ingredients, and Québec producer.
sources.supports: A current Québec-listed prepared pork product is named Cretons; its ingredient declaration lists pork, onions, pork leaf fat, and seasonings. Product-specific evidence corroborates current market identity and does not establish a general recipe or numeric conversion.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only Québec pork-based cretons / cretons. Keep rillettes, cretons de panne, generic pork pâté/spread, head cheese, and plant-based cretons-style products distinct. No recipe row or numeric behavior is inferred.

sources.title: Office québécois de la langue française, crosne du Japon (GDT)

sources.title: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, Plants of the World Online, Stachys affinis Bunge
sources.locator: Accepted name and common-name section
sources.supports: Accepts Stachys affinis Bunge and lists Japanese artichoke and crosnes de Japon among names associated with a synonym. Taxonomic and vernacular context only.

sources.title: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, ECOCROP, Stachys affinis
sources.locator: Brief description, uses, and common names
sources.supports: Describes small edible root tubers eaten boiled or fried and lists Chinese artichoke, Japanese artichoke, and crosne among common names. It gives no household measure.

sources.title: Agriculture Canada, Cultures de remplacement pour les Prairies
sources.locator: Crosne du Japon crop chapter, pp. 25–27
sources.supports: Names crosne du Japon and Stachys affinis, describes the edible tubers, and reports raw consumption in China and Japan. Crop dimensions and field yields remain agronomic and do not establish household measures.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only generic Stachys affinis tubers as Chinese artichoke / crosne du Japon, using the OQLF-supported bilingual names and narrow source-attested aliases. Keep globe artichoke and Jerusalem artichoke distinct. Reviewed sources support culinary use but no reusable household measure or substitution; add no forms, measures, conversions, yields, recipe links, or substitution rules.

sources.title: Office québécois de la langue française, croûton (GDT)
sources.locator: Definition, preferred French term, and English equivalent.

sources.supports: Uses croutons as a French product-family name for a lightly toasted and seasoned bread product; supports market wording, not a universal formulation.

Add the exact Canadian retail phrase stuffing croutons as an English alias on the existing crouton identity. Do not map unqualified stuffing cubes or all stuffing products to croutons; add no forms, measures, conversions, yields, or substitutions.

sources.locator: Definition, preferred French term, and English translation
sources.supports: Defines huile de palme as vegetable oil produced from the fruit pulp of the oil palm and gives palm oil as the English term. The entry does not specify crude or refined processing.

sources.title: Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency (Anvisa), Perguntas e respostas sobre óleos e gorduras vegetais
sources.locator: Question 25, denominations for vegetable oils and fats; explanation of IN 87/2021, Art. 3
sources.supports: States that azeite de dendê is an alternative denomination for crude palm oil or palm fat. This narrows the name to the crude product and does not establish synonymy with refined palm oil.

sources.title: Codex Alimentarius, CXS 210-1999, Standard for Named Vegetable Oils
sources.locator: Section 2, product definitions for palm oil, palm-kernel oil, palm olein, and palm stearin
sources.supports: Defines palm oil from the fleshy mesocarp, palm-kernel oil from the kernel, and olein/stearin as fractions. These are separate product boundaries; no process equivalence or substitution is inferred.

sources.title: Curvelo et al., Qualidade do óleo de palma bruto (Elaeis guineensis): matéria-prima para fritura de acarajés
sources.locator: Introduction, abstract, and study description of crude palm-oil products used by acarajé vendors in Salvador
sources.supports: Documents crude palm oil as the frying ingredient studied in Bahia acarajé production. Study-specific quality measurements are not transferred to the catalog.

sources.title: Anvisa, Materiais do diálogo setorial sobre atualização das listas de óleos e gorduras vegetais
sources.locator: Summary of the 2026-08-27 sector dialogue and stated next steps for updating IN 87/2021
sources.supports: Says an update to fatty-acid-composition ranges for palm oils and fractions is planned, with a draft still to be prepared and submitted. It does not report an enacted amendment to the azeite de dendê denomination.

decisions.reason: Add a distinct FAT_AND_OIL identity for crude palm oil, using crude palm oil in English and huile de palme brute (azeite de dendê) provisionally in French. Anvisa limits azeite de dendê to crude palm oil or fat; Codex separates mesocarp palm oil from kernel oil and palm fractions. Keep refined palm oil, palm-kernel oil, olein, stearin, and generic vegetable oil distinct. Add no aliases, forms, density, mappings, measurements, conversions, substitutions, or recipe links.

The French product wording remains provisional pending Québec culinary terminology review. Anvisa reports that composition ranges for palm oils and fractions are under planned regulatory update; its September 2026 notice describes next steps, not an enacted change to the azeite de dendê naming rule.

Keep it separate from stevia leaves and purified steviol glycosides. The descriptive French display is not a CFIA common-name ruling; no retail-food safety claim, aliases, form, measure, recipe link, conversion, yield, or substitution is added.
Present in the legacy RecipeKeeper catalog but absent from the canonical bundled seed; reconcile identity and aliases before acceptance.

sources.supports: Lists Cucurbita moschata leaves for food and beverage uses. Supports the species and plant-part boundary, not a particular recipe, handling method, Québec availability, or measurement.

sources.locator: Pumpkin profile identifying Cucurbita moschata and describing leaf use.

sources.title: USDA National Nutrient Database for Standard Reference, Release 28
sources.locator: Food Group 11 entries NDB 11418 (pumpkin leaves, raw) and NDB 11419 (pumpkin leaves, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt), including common measures and item taxon labels.
sources.supports: Reports one cup as 39 g for raw NDB 11418, whose item label lists no taxon, and one cup as 71 g for cooked NDB 11419, which lists Cucurbita spp. at genus level. Neither identifies Cucurbita moschata; retain the quantities with the exact USDA food entries and do not transfer them to this species-specific identity.

sources.title: FAO, Pacific Islands Food Composition Tables, second edition, food-code list
sources.locator: Vegetable food-code list, entries C048 raw pumpkin leaves and C025 boiled pumpkin leaves.
sources.supports: Identifies C048 and C025 as Cucurbita pepo. This taxonomic scope applies to the corresponding S05 composition entries and does not support transfer to Cucurbita moschata.

substitutionFindings.context: PROTA makes a broad Cucurbita moschata leaf-use replacement statement without naming a dish role, recipe, or preparation-state match.
substitutionFindings.basis: PROTA states that Cucurbita maxima leaves can substitute for the fruits, leaves, and seeds of Cucurbita moschata, while noting that C. maxima leaves are coarser and that this changes with cooking.
limitations: No target dish, ingredient role, preparation-state match, ratio, quantity basis, or adjustment is specified.
No Cucurbita maxima leaf reference is proposed in this review.
Do not create a universal replacement recommendation or active substitution rule from this broad source statement.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only musk pumpkin leaves / feuilles de courge musquée for the edible leaves of Cucurbita moschata. Keep aliases empty and the identity separate from fruit, seed, flower, C. maxima and C. pepo leaves, and Telfairia occidentalis (Ugu) leaves. Product and recipe amounts are not transferred; no form, measure, density, mapping, recipe link, conversion, yield, or active substitution is added.

No reusable household measure or species-specific density is supported for Cucurbita moschata leaves. USDA cup weights are attached to generic pumpkin-leaf entries (one with no taxon and one genus-level Cucurbita spp.), while the FAO composition entries are explicitly Cucurbita pepo; keep every value with its source food and add no measurement observation or mapping.

The PROTA Cucurbita maxima leaf replacement statement lacks a dish role, preparation-state match, ratio, or adjustment. Keep the finding blocked pending contextual evidence and add no active rule or recipe link.

sources.title: Bondarenko et al., Study of the influence of buckwheat flour and flax seeds on consumption properties of long-stored bakery products
sources.locator: Abstract; section 2, Table 1 and dark-flour preparation (journal pp. 9–12); section 3 and Table 3 (pp. 13–14); conclusion (p. 16).
sources.supports: The primary study describes one dark-buckwheat-flour sample made from peeled grain after hydrothermal steam processing. In one yeast-leavened wheat-bread formula intended for rusk production, it tests 15%, 20%, and 25% wheat-flour-mass replacement and reports lower volume and porosity at 20% and 25%, with 15% as the maximum for that formula. All preparation, percentages, moisture shares, and results remain specific to the study sample and formula; the paper does not establish equivalence to the catalog’s Québec identity or a category-level replacement rule.

substitutionFindings.context: One study’s hydrothermally processed dark-buckwheat-flour sample replacing wheat-flour mass in its yeast-leavened bread formula for rusk production.
substitutionFindings.basis: The study tests 15%, 20%, and 25% replacement and identifies 15% as the maximum within its formula after lower volume and porosity at the higher levels. This describes that sample and formula only.
limitations: The sample preparation is not established as equivalent to the Québec farine grise de sarrasin identity on this record.
The result does not establish a recommended percentage, upper limit, hydration adjustment, or substitution rule for dark buckwheat flour as a category or for other recipes.
Replacement percentages and dough-moisture shares are formula-specific evidence, not ingredient measures, density observations, or unit mappings.
No matching bundled recipe provides a role, amount, or method for a recipe-specific link.

sources.title: Deep N. Yadav, Krishna K. Singh, and Jagbir Rehal, Studies on fortification of wheat flour with defatted rice bran for chapati making
sources.locator: Abstract, Introduction, and Materials and methods; edible-grade defatted rice bran and chapati trials.
sources.supports: Identifies edible-grade defatted rice bran as a by-product of rice-bran oil extraction and uses an edible-grade sample from a local extraction unit in chapati research. Particle sizes, stabilization, blend percentages, and all sample and sensory results remain specific to the study; they do not establish a home-recipe ratio, kitchen measure, density, or general replacement advice.

sources.title: Sudha Sairam, A. G. Gopala Krishna, and Asna Urooj, Physico-chemical characteristics of defatted rice bran and its utilization in a bakery product
sources.locator: Abstract, Materials and methods, and bread trials.
sources.supports: Defines the study material as laboratory-extracted and commercial defatted rice-bran samples and investigates its use in bread. Sample properties, bulk-density and absorption results, extraction methods, and bread formulations remain tied to the named study samples and methods; they do not establish a generic consumer measure, density, or transferable blend ratio.

sources.title: FAO, Le riz dans la nutrition humaine — Valeur nutritionnelle du riz et des régimes alimentaires à base de riz
sources.locator: Section “Effet hypocholestérolémique du son de riz,” lines discussing “son de riz stabilisé et dégraissé.”
sources.supports: Attests the French wording “son de riz stabilisé et dégraissé.” This is used only as terminology evidence, not as a Québec-preferred compound, product definition, or human-food claim for the proposed identity.

substitutionFindings.context: Replacement of another ingredient with defatted rice bran in an unspecified recipe.
substitutionFindings.basis: The reviewed studies test source-specific defatted-rice-bran samples as partial ingredients in particular chapati and bread formulations. Their experimental blend levels, sample properties, and methods do not establish a reusable recipe substitution or adjustment.
limitations: Do not transfer study blend percentages or sample characteristics to other defatted rice bran or ordinary home recipes.
No reviewed source establishes a target ingredient, dish type, recipe role, preparation state, kitchen quantity, ratio, or adjustment for a reusable substitution.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only generic defatted rice bran / son de riz dégraissé in GRAIN_AND_CEREAL, separate from raw/general rice bran and rice-bran oil. Keep the descriptive French compound provisional and aliases empty. Study sample properties and formulation levels remain source-specific; add no forms, measurements, recipe links, conversions, yields, or active substitutions.
No reusable kitchen measure, mass-volume conversion, density, yield, or standard grade is supported. Laboratory and named-sample properties remain scoped to the studies.
The chapati and bread studies do not establish a generally applicable replacement ratio or adjustment; keep contextual substitution research blocked and add no active rule.

sources.supports: Describes wheat germ meal as a dry, defatted powder by-product of low-temperature CO₂ wheat-germ oil extraction and tests it in rye–wheat bread. The sample source, extraction, formula, percentages, hydration, and outcomes are specific to this study.

sources.title: M. U. Arshad, F. M. Anjum, and T. Zahoor, “Nutritional assessment of cookies supplemented with defatted wheat germ”

sources.supports: Tests wheat-flour replacement by defatted wheat germ in specific cookie formulas. Replacement levels and acceptability are sample- and study-specific; the rat-diet evaluation is not human nutrition guidance.

limitations: Keep all replacement percentages, particle sizes, moisture values, sample properties, and study outcomes attached to their cited experimental formulas.

The broader chickpea flour / farine de pois chiches queries return multiple qualified products, and pois chiches Desi returns the separate whole-pulse and flour rows. Keep whole Desi chickpeas, black/Kala Chana chickpeas, generic chickpea flour, and chana sattu distinct. decisions.reason: Add identity-only dill flower heads for the whole green/flexible umbel of correctly identified Anethum graveolens at the source-described pickling stage. Keep foliage, mature dill seed, pickles, infused liquids, and other preparations separate. The French display ombelles d’aneth is descriptive and provisional; the OQLF sources attest only its component terms. Recipe quantities and maturity instructions remain source-specific. Add no forms, measurements, recipe links, conversions, yields, or substitutions.

sources.title: OQLF, aneth (GDT; AFNOR entry)

sources.title: CFIA, Canadian Food Compositional Standards, Volume 6, section 6.1.17

sources.supports: Defines dill seed, whole or ground, as the dried fruit of Anethum graveolens L. or Anethum sowa D.C. Supports the identity and ground-form boundary; compositional limits are not used as recipe measures.

sources.title: Provigo Québec, le Choix du Président Graines d’aneth, 50 g

sources.supports: Provides a Québec retail listing with the exact French plural name graines d’aneth and explicitly describes the seeds as usable whole or crushed. The package mass is not generalized into a household measure.

sources.title: Provigo Canada, President’s Choice Dill Seeds listing
sources.locator: Spices and Seasonings category listing for President’s Choice Dill Seeds, 50 g.
sources.supports: Uses the English plural product title Dill Seeds for a whole seed spice. Supports the English plural search alias only, not a household measure.

sources.locator: Spices and Seasonings category listing with the French product title graines d’aneth moulues.

sources.title: Provigo Canada, Dion Herbs & Spices Ground Dill Seed, 30 g

sources.supports: Supports the English name and dry ground form label. The package mass is not generalized into a household measure.

decisions.reason: Add the source-supported culinary seed identity as dill seed / graines d’aneth, with only the attested English plural alias and one dry ground form. Do not assign bare dill or aneth because an active broad dill-herb reference already owns those labels. Keep whole and ground seed wording within the CFIA identity boundary; add no density, unit mapping, measurement, recipe link, conversion, yield, or substitution.

decisions.reason: Add standalone Korean doenjang as an identity-only fermented soybean paste. Keep miso, Chinese soybean pastes, ganjang/soy sauce, Tojang, and prepared stew/soup products separate; one manufacturer formula is not generalized.

sources.title: Hongyan Yang et al., Dominant Microorganisms during the Spontaneous Fermentation of Suan Cai, a Chinese Fermented Vegetable
sources.locator: Introduction and materials-and-methods description of suan cai in Northeast China.
sources.supports: Describes suan cai as a traditional Northeast China Chinese-cabbage preserve. The 1% salt, 750 L jar, one-month fermentation, and laboratory results describe this article’s process and do not define a universal formula, measure, or safety instruction.

sources.title: M. Xiao et al., The microbial communities and flavour compounds of Jiangxi yancai, Sichuan paocai and Dongbei suancai: Three major types of traditional Chinese fermented vegetables
sources.locator: Title and abstract naming the three traditional fermented-vegetable types.
sources.supports: Treats Dongbei suancai as one named traditional Chinese fermented-vegetable type alongside Jiangxi yancai and Sichuan paocai. Supports keeping these regional preserve identities distinct; it does not establish a universal formula or transferable method.

sources.title: Yuan Liu et al., Characterization of the microbial communities and their correlations with volatile flavor compounds and physicochemical factors in Bashang suancai, a traditional Chinese pickle
sources.locator: Introduction distinguishing Bashang and Dongbei suancai by region, cabbage type, and fermentation season.
sources.supports: Distinguishes Bashang suancai from Dongbei suancai by region and raw cabbage type. The study’s Bashang recipe, process, salt level, season, and measurements remain specific to Bashang and do not define Dongbei preparation.

sources.title: Office québécois de la langue française, Grand dictionnaire terminologique, chou de Chine
sources.locator: Entry title, definition, and French terms for raw Chinese cabbage.
sources.supports: Supports the Québec French term for raw Chinese cabbage only. It does not name Dongbei suancai or establish a French term for this preserve.

substitutionFindings.context: Replacement of finished Dongbei suancai in an unspecified recipe role and preparation state.
substitutionFindings.basis: The reviewed sources establish a regional preserved-food identity and process-specific studies, but no source recommends a replacement for finished Dongbei suancai in a defined dish role, method, or amount.
limitations: Do not infer replacement by raw napa cabbage, generic pickled mustard greens, mei gan cai, zha cai, Yibin ya cai, kimchi, Bashang suancai, Jiangxi yancai, or Sichuan paocai from shared cabbage, fermentation, or condiment wording.
Do not transfer the 1% salt, 750 L jar, one-month fermentation, or laboratory values from the 2014 study, or the Bashang process findings, to other preparations.
No reviewed source establishes a target dish, role, preparation state, quantity basis, ratio, or adjustment for a contextual substitution rule.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only generic Dongbei suancai for the region-qualified Northeast Chinese fermented cabbage preserve. Keep the French display as a provisional borrowed name and do not add broad suan cai, Chinese sauerkraut, or pickled-cabbage aliases. Preserve raw Napa cabbage, other named regional preserves, and all existing branded entries; add no forms, measures, recipe links, conversions, yields, or active substitutions.

The reviewed process studies do not establish a transferable serving measure, mass-volume conversion, density, unit mapping, yield, or preparation-independent amount. Keep every salt ratio, batch size, fermentation period, and laboratory value within its exact source context.
No reviewed evidence recommends a substitute for finished Dongbei suancai in a defined dish role. Keep the finding blocked and add no active contextual rule or recipe-line link.

decisions.reason: Accept identity-only dongchimi as a generic named Korean kimchi type with the source-attested English alias radish water kimchi. Keep it distinct from generic kimchi, kkakdugi, pickled radish, and other named types. Use dongchimi as a provisional borrowed French display because the reviewed OQLF entry supports only the parent term kimchi. Keep the official example recipe amounts and method source-specific. Add no form, recipe link, measure, density, mapping, conversion, yield, or substitution.

sources.locator: Product title, product description, cooking uses, and pickup information
sources.supports: A Toronto-area retailer uses 大地魚粉 for a seasoning powder listed for noodles, soups, congee, vegetables, and meat. Seller origin, purity, and undefined small-spoon statements are not treated as verified product specifications or reusable measures. No ingredient panel or species is given.

sources.supports: The restaurant describes its broth as containing dried flounder fish powder; the paired Chinese description names 大地魚 but does not repeat 粉. Supports local culinary use and the exact English phrase, not a packaged formulation or species determination.

sources.locator: Page 6, chef’s note 8; page 7 ingredient list and method
sources.supports: The official recipe describes baking dried 大地魚 flesh until crisp and grinding it to make 大地魚粉, then using the powder for savoury flavour in lotus-root patties. Culinary-use evidence for the named product concept, not a retail-product formulation or species assignment.

sources.locator: Termes utilisés dans certains contextes; common-language term and included fish families
sources.supports: The 2026 terminology entry lists poissons plats as a common-context term and includes plies, soles, turbots, and halibuts. Supports descriptive French wording and the multi-species boundary, not the fish species in any package.

sources.title: Kwan Kee Bamboo Noodle, All Products
sources.locator: Indexed retail product listing: Kwan Kee Dried Flounder Fish Powder Retail Bottle
sources.supports: The indexed Kwan Kee retail collection names a Dried Flounder Fish Powder Retail Bottle. The reviewed snapshot marked it sold out and direct page opening returned a cache miss. Supports the English product term only, not current availability, ingredients, measure, or species.

sources.title: Hong Kong Centre for Food Safety, List of Small Volume Exemption Products
sources.locator: Generated 2026-10-16; page 26, product record 21-006404
sources.supports: The current government list pairs Chinese brand and food names 安記海味 / 安記大地魚粉 with English On Kee / On Kee Dried Flatfish Powder. Supports a product-name crosswalk for the powder class; it is not an ingredient declaration or species determination for the T&T item.

decisions.reason: Add dried flatfish powder / poudre de poissons plats séchés as a species-neutral PROTEIN product identity for this named dried-flatfish powder class. Add only the exact English alias dried flounder fish powder. Keep it separate from generic fish powder, Bonga powder, dried bonito powder, and the flounder and sole market-name groups. Do not infer a species, package composition, measure, density, form, unit mapping, conversion, yield, recipe link, warning, or substitution. No bundled recipe demand was found.

sources.title: FAO/WHO Codex Alimentarius, Norme régionale sur les feuilles fraîches de Gnetum spp. (Afrique), CXS 335R-2020
sources.locator: Sections 1 and 6.1 and footnote 2.
sources.supports: Covers fresh whole or sliced Gnetum spp. leaves and names the two main African commercial species, G. africanum and G. bucholzianum. Its country-specific local-name examples support a genus-level leaf product and caution against global aliases; it does not standardize dried leaves or a Québec French term.

sources.title: FAO, Gnetum domestication for livelihood improvement and conservation
sources.locator: Introduction and Importance of Gnetum.
sources.supports: Describes edible leaves of G. africanum and G. buchholzianum in West and Central African trade, reports regional name variation, and says the commercial species are not distinguishable. This is regional ethnobotanical evidence, not a retail specification or Québec language ruling.

sources.title: Plant Resources of Tropical Africa (PROTA), Gnetum africanum
sources.locator: Uses; Production and international trade; Adulterations and substitutes.
sources.supports: States that shredded leaves can be dried and preserved, that the two African Gnetum species are often mixed in trade, and that dried shredded leaves are exported. Its qualitative substitute notes do not establish a global alias, household measure, or substitution ratio.

sources.title: AFFOXY, Okok séché / Okazi / Fomboua
sources.locator: Current Québec product title and description.
sources.supports: A Québec retailer describes finely shredded dried Gnetum africanum leaves from Cameroon and uses the descriptive French wording feuille séchée de Gnetum africanum. Its local-name title and 50/100/200 g package options are listing-specific and are not global aliases or reusable measures.

sources.title: AFFOXY, Notre histoire
sources.locator: Company background and location.
sources.supports: Identifies AFFOXY as a Québec-based seller of Cameroon foods. Supports Québec-facing retail context only, not terminology authority or a product specification.

sources.title: SAVANNA SELECT, Dried ERU Leaves (Okok) 100 g
sources.locator: Current product page title, description, and bilingual product details.
sources.supports: A Canadian bilingual listing identifies dried Gnetum africanum leaves and uses Dried ERU Leaves (Okok) with a French product heading for dried Eru leaves. Its 100 g SKU, serving suggestion, water-rehydration claim, and preparation advice remain source-specific and are not active catalog measures or rules.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only dried Gnetum leaves / feuilles séchées de Gnetum as a genus-level dried leaf ingredient. Keep eru, okok, okazi, fumbwa, afang, ukasi, koko, and species binomials out of global aliases because the names are regional, ambiguous, or do not establish species-pure trade lots. Add no forms, measures, density, mappings, conversions, yields, recipe links, or substitutions.

sources.title: ICAR-Central Coastal Agricultural Research Institute, Crop: Kokum
sources.locator: Scientific name, common/local names, and post-harvest management.
sources.supports: Identifies Kokum as Garcinia indica, gives Bhirand/Sola/Kokum as common or local names, and lists Agal, Sol khadi, kokum butter, and rind powder among distinct post-harvest products. Does not establish a kitchen measure or universal rind process.

sources.title: Indian Institute of Spices Research, Garcinia
sources.locator: Crop overview and common-variety names.
sources.supports: States that dried Garcinia rind is used as a souring agent and identifies Kokum as G. indica separately from Malabar tamarind (Garcinia cambogia). The page covers more than one Garcinia crop and supplies no recipe measure.

sources.title: Zaika Foods, Zaika Kokum
sources.locator: Product title, 200 g package listing, and product description.
sources.supports: A Canadian product page titled Zaika Kokum describes dried, salted rind used as a curry condiment. The listed 200 g is package size only, not a portion or conversion.

sources.title: Table Indienne, Kokum (Amsul), Écorce acidulée du Konkan
sources.locator: French-language product title and description; uses and tamarind comparison.
sources.supports: Identifies kokum/amsul as dried Garcinia indica rind and uses kokum séché in French. The retailer suggests replacing tamarind in most recipes at roughly equivalent quantity and mentions coconut-based dishes broadly, but gives no recipe-level role, method, preparation state, or salt adjustment; no substitution rule is inferred. The retailer is in France, not Québec.

sources.title: Spices Board of India, Kokam
sources.locator: Kokam commodity entry; botanical name, commercial part, uses, and Indian names.
sources.supports: Names Garcinia indica, identifies cured fruit peel as the commercial part, and states that the dried and salted rind is used as a condiment in curries. The page lists Kokam and Amsol spellings; it does not establish a household measure or universal recipe.

sources.title: Health Canada, Groupes de cultures et propriétés chimiques de leurs résidus
sources.locator: French-language list, entry Kokum (Garcinia indica).
sources.supports: The Canadian French-language page includes Kokum (Garcinia indica). Supports the borrowed French plant name and species association only, not a culinary product definition or terminology recommendation.

substitutionFindings.context: A French-language retailer suggests using dried kokum rind instead of tamarind in most recipes at roughly equivalent quantity and mentions coconut-based dishes broadly, but does not define a specific recipe, ingredient role, cooking method, preparation state, or salt adjustment.
substitutionFindings.basis: The broad product suggestion lacks recipe-level scope and a defined quantity basis, so it cannot support a global or contextual substitution rule.
limitations: Keep the retailer suggestion as blocked evidence; do not apply it as a recipe-line replacement.

decisions.reason: Accept dried kokum rind / écorce séchée de kokum as a distinct Garcinia indica dried-rind souring spice. Add only kokam, kokum séché, and amsul as search aliases. Keep Malabar tamarind, goraka, tamarind, juices, butter, powders, syrups, and prepared drinks separate. Retail package weight is not a recipe measure. Record the broad tamarind-replacement suggestion as blocked pending context; add no active substitution, form, conversion, yield, or recipe link.

sources.title: OQLF, zeste d'orange déshydraté (GDT)

decisions.reason: Add dried orange zest / zeste d'orange déshydraté as a species-qualified zest product, separate from generic citrus zest, lemon zest, and full orange peel. Do not generalize to all dried citrus peel or candied citrus products. No form, measurement, conversion, yield, or substitution data is inferred.

sources.locator: CNF 2026 relational files and 2015 online access notice.

These source-specific portions do not establish a current CNF 2026 value, the form or brand used by the bundled recipes, or a common spoon capacity and fill method. Keep measurement research blocked; add no active density, unit mapping, or recipe-line conversion.

sources.title: Nayi et al., Rehydration modeling and characterization of dehydrated sweet corn, Food Science & Nutrition 11(6), 2023
sources.locator: Materials and Methods sections 2.3–2.4 and Results section 3.1; compare with Conclusion section 4.
sources.supports: Primary study of one Madhuri variety. Kernels were blanched and tray-dried at 55–70 °C, then rehydrated in boiling water. Results report separate rehydration-ratio ranges for control (2.88–3.54), hot-water-blanched (2.56–3.46), steam-blanched (2.23–3.13), and microwave-blanched (2.56–2.65) samples. The paper conclusion inconsistently reports an overall 2.56–3.54 range. None is a general kitchen yield or measure.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only edible crab / tourteau for Cancer pagurus with English aliases brown crab and common crab. Keep forms, recipe links, density, and mappings empty.

No reusable household measure, density, unit mapping, or yield is supported: the distributor package and biological yield discussion are product- or species-specific, while Metro supplies a taxon-unresolved recipe amount. Record measurement research as no supported value and substitution research as no supported substitute; add no forms, conversions, yields, recipe links, or active substitution rules.

decisions.reason: Keep unqualified eel / anguille unresolved as a global identity. CFIA applies Eel / Anguille to multiple Anguilla species and separately lists Conger Eel; OQLF’s Québec food-fish entry scopes anguille to American eel. Québec and Canadian product listings show local smoked eel and distinct unagi/anago products but provide no species-level link for those products. No eel term appears in the bundled recipe corpus. Retain ingredient-ref-american-eel unchanged; add no generic reference, alias, form, measurement, recipe link, conversion, yield, or substitution. The current query eel result is the species row’s own display-name match, not a generic identity.

Promote the held candidate in place to an identity-only, visibly qualified name group for the exact repeated CFIA label Eel / Anguille across the three listed Anguilla species. This name group is not a taxon or culinary-equivalence claim. Keep the bare Québec term anguille on American eel / Anguilla rostrata; keep American eel, smoked eel, short-finned eel, Conger, unagi, anago, and kabayaki distinct. Preserve the prior unresolved decision as history, and keep all product-specific sources and claims attached to their original scope. Add no forms, measurements, density, mappings, conversions, yields, recipe links, or substitutions.

sources.supports: Reports 12 raw sample-group averages for UK shell-on medium and large size bands. Each raw subsample uses 24 eggs. Table values are averages; the result ranges are across group means, not individual-egg extrema. Detailed collection dates conflict with the summary 2011 date.

sources.title: Hisasaga, Griffin, and Tarrant, Survey of egg quality in commercially available table eggs
sources.locator: Materials and methods; Tables 1–2
sources.supports: Measures shell, yolk, and albumen weights for six US retail brands and reports brand means. Egg size class is not stated; total weight includes shell; Table 1 brand counts sum to 306 although methods say 309 eggs, and Table 2 does not define its ± statistic. Ranges over means are not individual-egg intervals.

sources.title: University of Maine Cooperative Extension, Using Egg Substitutes in Baking and Cooking
sources.locator: Egg Substitutes in Baking introduction and seltzer-water row.
sources.supports: Reports a test of substitutes in a yellow-cake recipe calling for two eggs and gives 1/4 cup seltzer water per egg. Seltzer had the best texture and flavor among tested substitutes but produced pale color. Does not establish muffin transfer, egg size, or the exact mixing method in recipe 069.

sources.title: King Arthur Baking, No eggs? Here’s your guide for substituting
sources.locator: Sparkling water or seltzer entry and Basic Muffin comparison.
sources.supports: Gives 1/4 cup (57 g) sparkling water per egg, calls the substitution hit-or-miss, and cautions that it does not blend well when eggs are creamed with butter. Reports one Basic Muffin test where sparkling-water muffins were similar to the egg control; results may vary by formula. The 57 g is the source mass for the sparkling-water amount, not egg mass.

decisions.reason: Removed source-less draft density and unit-mapping values from the active bundled catalog. Restore a value only with source, exact food/form, unit convention, method or basis, and reviewer disposition.

Record FDC 748967 food_portion 193781 as a source-specific published count-weight observation only. Retain the item's Grade A, Large designation and exact portion modifier; do not infer a cross-market size mapping, variability range, density, or active runtime conversion. The FDC item description does not explicitly identify species.

CNF, USDA SR28/HG72, and FDC publish distinct source and market bases. FDC 748967 adds 50.3 g for one Grade A, Large egg with modifier whole without shell; the RACC portion is not an egg-count measure. Preserve each edible count portion by source and size; no source-neutral large-egg mass, cross-market size equivalence, shell-on-to-edible factor, density, or runtime count mapping is justified. The FDC portion row does not report count-weight variability.

Store UK sample-group and US brand-mean spreads as source-bounded derived observed_sample_range evidence. These ranges describe published group/brand means, not individual-egg minima/maxima, do not establish a common size class or market mapping, and do not resolve exact recipe-state matches. Keep runtime density, count mapping, and conversions blocked.

Record the source-backed one-way egg-to-plain-sparkling-water candidate for selected light, fluffy muffin batters as blocked pending recipe-specific evidence. The family recipe 069 combines egg with margarine and brown sugar, while the sources do not establish whether its method fits the substitution. Do not create an active rule or recipe-line substitution link.

substitutionFindings.context: Selected baking uses named by the source, including meringue and single-layer/snacking cakes; not a universal replacement for every cake or cookie.
substitutionFindings.basis: 1/4 cup (57 g) aquafaba per 1 egg, preserving the source-published volume and mass values.
expectedEffects: Aquafaba can whip to a meringue-like foam.
It provides little structure to baked goods.
limitations: Aquafaba has no accepted ingredient reference ID in the current catalog.
The active resolver cannot represent count-to-volume or count-to-mass replacement quantities with this recipe-function scope.
Do not generalize the source to all cakes or cookies.

substitutionFindings.context: One-way egg-to-plain-sparkling-water candidate for the single whole-egg line in bundled recipe 069, limited to selected light, fluffy muffin batters where the egg is mixed with liquids and then incorporated into dry ingredients. Recipe 069 combines the egg with margarine and brown sugar; its instructions do not establish whether this is a creamed-fat method.
substitutionFindings.basis: University of Maine Extension gives 1/4 cup seltzer per egg in its tested two-egg yellow cake. King Arthur gives 1/4 cup (57 g) sparkling water per egg and reports a similar result in one Basic Muffin comparison. Store the 1/4 cup volume-to-count basis. The 57 g is King Arthur’s mass for the same sparkling-water quantity, not egg mass; source egg size is unstated, while recipe 069 calls for one large egg.
expectedEffects: King Arthur says the sparkling-water option can be hit-or-miss; its one Basic Muffin test was very similar to the egg control.
In the tested yellow cake, UMaine Extension reports seltzer had the best texture and flavor among tested substitutes but produced pale color.
limitations: The exact family muffin recipe has not been tested with sparkling water, and its margarine/egg mixing method is not sufficiently described to confirm fit with the source examples.
Do not infer a mass-for-mass amount, a source-neutral egg-size mapping, or an adjustment to the other liquids, leaveners, bake time, or yield.
Use plain, unflavoured sparkling water only; exclude sweetened or flavoured carbonated drinks, tonic, club soda, and bare soda.
Do not reverse the direction or generalize to other muffin, cake, quick-bread, egg-heavy, custard, soufflé, sponge, chiffon, angel-food, or foam-based recipes.
Keep out of runtime because the current rule model cannot preserve the count-to-volume basis and enforce the required recipe method.

decisions.reason: Accept identity-only egg noodles / nouilles aux œufs as a finished noodle-product identity. Do not store nouilles aux oeufs as an alias because the ingredient-search normalizer folds the œ/oe spelling to the same key as the display; the unligature spelling remains searchable. Keep generic pasta, ramen, rice noodles, instant noodles, and egg-roll wrappers separate. Current Québec and federal sources support the bilingual name; current ramen products show both egg-containing and no-egg products. Add no form, recipe link, density, unit mapping, measurement, conversion, yield, or substitution.

substitutionFindings.basis: The study uses Monlis and Norberto Triticum monococcum bran, laboratory-ground through a 0.5 mm outlet grid, with common-wheat type 00 flour. decisions.reason: Add generic einkorn bran / son de petit épeautre for the bran fraction of cultivated Triticum monococcum. The primary food study supports einkorn bran as a human-food milling fraction; TERMIUM and the Québec mill support the base name petit épeautre, while the French bran compound is directly attested by a manufacturer listing and remains provisional for Québec. Keep spelt bran, wheat bran, einkorn flour, einkorn berries, and unresolved wholegrain einkorn semolina separate. Do not transfer product details or study measurements. Add no aliases, forms, measures, density, mappings, recipe links, conversions, yields, or active substitutions.

Record the 2025 bread trial as a source-bounded substitution finding only. The 20% level, sample genotypes, laboratory grinding, flour, process, and individually optimized water do not support a reusable recipe rule or recommendation.

sources.supports: Lists European Lake Yellow Perch IQF fillets, describes European lake fisheries, and prices the item by the pound. The page provides no scientific name, French title, standardized package mass, or species-to-CFIA crosswalk; the listing is not assigned to Perca fluviatilis.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only Eurasian perch / perche européenne for Perca fluviatilis, with European perch and European Yellow Perch as the only English aliases. CFIA gives the Canadian bilingual fish-label name pair and separately assigns European Yellow Perch to TSN 168470; ITIS and the European Commission corroborate Eurasian/European perch and European perch. Keep broad perch, perche, yellow perch, perchaude, perche commune, river perch, and the scientific name out of aliases. The CFIA alternate label intentionally makes the broad query yellow perch return both Perca species; no generic perch query is represented as uniquely resolved.

Use CFIA’s qualified Canadian French display perche européenne. OQLF maps bare perche to Perca fluviatilis but labels that term France and does not establish it as a Québec consumer fish name; do not describe perche européenne as an OQLF-preferred term. Keep French aliases empty.

No reusable portion, density, volume mapping, or package yield is supported. The Ontario retailer item is sold by the pound but gives no fixed package mass or scientific identification. Add no measurement observations, form, density, unit mapping, conversion, package yield, or recipe link.

No bundled recipe demand or reviewed source supports a directed substitution to another fish. Keep substitution research recorded as no supported substitute, with no global conversion, contextual rule, warning, or recipe-line link.

sources.title: Office québécois de la langue française, GDT, huître plate
sources.locator: Preferred-term, linked English/Latin records, note, and English translation fields.
sources.supports: In the food / edible-mollusk domain, designates huître plate as the preferred Québec term, links it to European flat oyster and Ostrea edulis, and lists European oyster and flat oyster as English translations. Notes commercial potential in Québec. Says belon and huître belon were not retained by the fish-products terminology committee.

sources.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, CFIA Fish List output for Ostrea edulis
sources.locator: Rows for TSN 79885: Ostrea edulis, European Oyster / Huître Plate, and generic Oyster / Edible Oyster / Huître entries.
sources.supports: Associates TSN 79885 and Ostrea edulis with European Oyster / Huître Plate. The same taxon also has generic Oyster / Edible Oyster / Huître entries; nearby Ostrea lurida rows also carry generic Oyster / Huître. This source is the CFIA Fish List common-name output, not an app alias list.

sources.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, Labelling requirements for fish and fish products
sources.locator: Common name and CFIA Fish List guidance sections.
sources.supports: CFIA says Fish List names are considered acceptable common names and their use is recommended; it says the list associates each species with a TSN and related hazards. This supports interpreting S02 as common-name guidance and does not claim that European flat oyster is the exact Fish List wording.

sources.title: Seafood Depot, Belon Oysters
sources.locator: Product title and binomial; characteristics, availability note, and Vaughan contact address.
sources.supports: Lists Belon Oysters / Ostrea edulis. The page says the item is fresh, harvested in France, product of France, 100 count per case, 1.5–3.5 inches in size, and available weather permitting; the supplier contact address is in Vaughan, Ontario. This is Canadian-supplier product evidence, not a stock guarantee or Québec retailer listing. Its count and size are SKU-specific and do not support a reusable culinary measure or yield.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only European flat oyster / huître plate for Ostrea edulis, with the source-backed qualified English alternate European oyster. Keep Belon as supplier-specific wording, broad oyster / huître terms out of aliases, the generic fresh-oyster candidate unresolved, and the Olympia decision separate.

No reusable kitchen measure, edible yield, ingredient form, or species substitution is supported. Keep the supplier’s fresh state, case count, and shell-size range as listing-specific evidence only; add no measurement observation, form, density, unit mapping, conversion, package yield, or substitution finding.

sources.title: Office québécois de la langue française, homard européen | Grand dictionnaire terminologique
sources.locator: Edible-crustacean domain, preferred French and English terms, definition, and Latin name
sources.supports: Pairs homard européen and European lobster with Homarus gammarus in an edible-crustacean entry. The broader homard and lobster terms are source alternatives but are not catalog aliases because they already belong to the American-lobster row and CFIA scopes them there for Canadian labeling.

sources.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, Susceptible species of aquatic animals
sources.locator: Crustacean table entries for Homarus americanus and Homarus gammarus; introductory scope note
sources.supports: Distinguishes Homarus gammarus as European lobster and H. americanus as American lobster; CFIA states that this aquatic-animal-health list does not replace the Fish List for food labeling.

sources.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, Fish List
sources.locator: Searchable CFIA Fish List records for TSN 97314, Homarus americanus
sources.supports: Search results list American Lobster / Homard Américain and the unqualified Lobster / Homard under H. americanus; the current list search returns no H. gammarus or European Lobster record. This is a Canadian labeling boundary.

sources.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, Guidance on determining the common names for fish sold or processed in Canada
sources.locator: Sections 1–4, scope, common-name definition, and Fish List use
sources.supports: Explains that the CFIA Fish List collects common names used for fish labeling in Canada and that the names listed for a species should be used for fish sold or processed in Canada; this proposal does not claim the European-lobster catalog display is an approved Canadian label.

sources.title: World Link Food Distributors, European Lobster product page

sources.supports: A Nova Scotia seafood distributor identifies a live European-lobster product as Homarus gammarus and describes year-round availability. The 30 lb case is a dated wholesale package observation, not current Québec retail availability, a kitchen measure, or a reusable conversion.

decisions.reason: Add the qualified Homarus gammarus identity under European lobster / homard européen. Keep unqualified lobster and homard on the existing American-lobster row; add no forms, measures, mappings, conversions, yields, recipe links, or substitutions.

sources.title: OQLF, sardine (GDT)
sources.locator: Québec edible-fish entry; term, English equivalents, and Latin name.

sources.locator: Rows for Sardina pilchardus and Sardinops sagax and additional Sardine / Pilchard entries, including species from Sardinella and Engraulis.

sources.locator: Current-name and common-name fields.
sources.supports: Identifies Sardina pilchardus and records European sardine and European pilchard common-name variants. Taxonomy/name evidence only.

sources.locator: FAO common names for Sardina pilchardus.
sources.supports: Lists European pilchard / sardine européenne for Sardina pilchardus. Supports a species-qualified bilingual display; it does not set a Québec regulatory label.

sources.title: CFIA, Guidance on determining the common names for fish sold or processed in Canada
sources.locator: Sections 3.2 and 4.
sources.supports: Explains that accepted common names in the Fish List are tied to individual fish species. It does not treat different listed species or products as interchangeable.

sources.locator: Sections 1–2, scope and product definition.
sources.supports: Defines canned sardine/sardine-type products made from multiple species and packed in water, oil, or another suitable medium. International product-class evidence only; not a Canadian species-equivalence rule.

sources.title: CFIA, Labelling requirements for fish and fish products
sources.locator: Sections “Fish oils” and “Descriptive words about the true nature of fish products.”
sources.supports: Distinguishes fish-oil products from fish meat and describes form, packing-medium, and condition descriptors for packaged fish products. Label guidance only; no ingredient conversion is established.

sources.title: FAO, Sardina pilchardus species sheet
sources.locator: Fishing and utilization section.
sources.supports: Reports distinct market preparations for Sardina pilchardus, including fresh/chilled, salted, smoked, marinated, canned, oil, fish meal, and bait. Trade-use examples only; no recipe measurement or conversion is derived.

decisions.reason: Scope this identity to Sardina pilchardus using European pilchard / sardine européenne. Keep bare sardine and pilchard names out of aliases; do not infer canned, oil-packed, salted, smoked, dried, marinated, or other forms. Add no recipe links, measurements, yields, conversions, or substitutions.

sources.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, Fish List query for European Smelt
sources.locator: Fish List rows for Osmerus eperlanus TSN 162039 and Osmerus mordax TSN 162041.
sources.supports: Lists O. eperlanus as European Smelt / éperlan Européen and O. mordax under Rainbow Smelt, Smelt, American Smelt / éperlan De Lac, and Lake Smelt. The Fish List reports a 2023-09-18 modification date. This supports Canadian fish-name and taxon identity, not a Québec product species or culinary interchangeability.

sources.locator: Fish List purpose and species-specific common-name guidance.

sources.title: Office québécois de la langue française, GDT: éperlan (FAO terminology entry)
sources.locator: Food-fish terminology pair authored by FAO in 1972.
sources.supports: Pairs éperlan / smelt with O. eperlanus in an older food-fish terminology record. This is not a current Québec fish-product normalization decision or evidence that a local product is this species.

sources.locator: Entry last updated 2011; normalized Québec term, translations, and commercialization note.

sources.title: FinFish Inc., European smelt product
sources.locator: Species identification, European dressed-smelt description, and boat-run bulk pack; company location cross-checked on the company page.
sources.supports: Canadian supplier page identifies O. eperlanus as European dressed smelt. Supplier evidence supports the species as an edible product, not Québec retail supply, a general ingredient form, package conversion, or measure.

sources.title: Mayrand, Éperlan entier frais, product 52958
sources.locator: Québec retail product page; approximate 1 kg unit and availability text observed on access.
sources.supports: Uses generic éperlan and an approximate package weight; the page showed Bientôt disponible and gives no species, binomial, or harvest origin. It supports local generic wording only and does not assign this product to O. eperlanus or establish a reusable measure.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only European smelt / éperlan européen for Osmerus eperlanus with empty alias arrays. Keep bare smelt and éperlan searchable through the two qualified species displays, and do not assign Mayrand’s generic éperlan item to this species. No forms, measures, mappings, recipe links, conversions, yields, or substitutions are supported.

sources.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, current Fish List tuna query
sources.locator: Unique common-name rows for TSN 172405 (Euthynnus lineatus) and TSN 172401 (Katsuwonus pelamis).
sources.supports: Shows overlapping Skipjack and Listao names across both taxa, alongside qualified Black Skipjack Tuna / Thon and Thonine Noire / Listao wording. Current Canadian common-name crosswalk, not proof of every retail SKU or a picker policy.

sources.title: Integrated Taxonomic Information System, Euthynnus lineatus, TSN 172405
sources.locator: Valid species and English/French common names.
sources.supports: Identifies E. lineatus as a valid species and lists black skipjack and thonine noire common names. Taxonomic authority, not Canadian product-label evidence.

sources.title: Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission, Euthynnus lineatus (BKJ)
sources.locator: Species identity and fisheries common name.
sources.supports: Identifies E. lineatus as Black skipjack tuna and distinguishes it from K. pelamis. Fisheries source, not Québec retail terminology.

sources.title: Office québécois de la langue française, GDT: thonine
sources.locator: Preferred Québec term, English equivalent, Latin name, and dated note about thon.
sources.supports: Links thonine to black skipjack and E. lineatus; the 1983 entry supports qualified Québec terminology but not the current full Thonine noire spelling, which is taken from CFIA.

sources.title: Health Canada, Canadian Nutrient File food code 3082 serving portions
sources.locator: Raw skipjack portion and refuse fields; CNF search context for the absence of an established E. lineatus code in this review.
sources.supports: Code 3082 is raw fresh K. pelamis only: 100 g edible portion=100 g, half fillet=98 g, Food Guide serving=90 g, and total refuse=65%. These are code-specific observations and are not transferred to E. lineatus or canned products.

decisions.reason: Add the identity-only qualified display Black skipjack tuna (Listao) / Thonine noire (thon) for E. lineatus at the same time as K. pelamis. The qualified labels let shared skipjack, skipjack tuna, and listao searches return both taxa while black skipjack tuna and thonine noire remain specific. Keep aliases empty and do not infer a product form or recipe link.
No E. lineatus-specific portion or conversion value was found in the bounded review. Do not transfer CNF code 3082 raw K. pelamis observations to this species or a canned product.

sources.title: CFIA, Canadian Food Compositional Standards
sources.locator: Sections 7.1.6–7.1.9.
sources.supports: Defines evaporated milk as milk with water removed and distinguishes it from sweetened condensed milk, evaporated skim milk, and evaporated partly skimmed milk. The composition limits are used only to define identity boundaries; no values are imported into active catalog data.

sources.title: ACIA, Normes d'identité canadiennes : Volume 1 - Produits laitiers
sources.locator: Sections 3-6, lait condensé, lait évaporé, lait écrémé évaporé, and lait évaporé partiellement écrémé.
sources.supports: The Canadian French dairy standard uses `lait évaporé ou lait concentré` for the standard evaporated-milk class and defines separate sweetened-condensed, evaporated-skim, and evaporated-partly-skimmed classes. No active composition data is added.

sources.title: Carnation, Lait évaporé
sources.locator: Current French product page title and product description.
sources.supports: The Canadian manufacturer uses `Lait évaporé` as the current product title and describes the product as milk with about half the water of ordinary milk. This confirms local product wording and product class, not an exact recipe substitution or reusable quantity.

sources.title: OQLF, produit laitier concentré
sources.locator: Definition and terminology note.
sources.supports: The entry prefers the broad term `produit laitier concentré` and calls `lait évaporé` and `lait condensé` improper generic terms. It explains that evaporated milk is a concentrated milk product while sweetened condensed milk is concentrated and sweetened; it does not define the current standardized retail product name.

decisions.reason: Removed source-less draft density and unit-mapping values from the active bundled catalog. Restore a value only with source, exact food/form, unit convention, method or basis, and reviewer disposition.

Verify the existing evaporated-milk identity as the Canadian standardized milk product from which water has been removed. Keep it distinct from sweetened condensed milk and the evaporated skim and partly skimmed classes. Retain the existing bilingual display `evaporated milk / lait évaporé`: the French Canadian standard and current Canadian manufacturer use that specific product name, while OQLF's older `produit laitier concentré` entry is broader. Do not add `lait concentré` or `lait condensé` as aliases. No forms, active measures, recipe links, conversions, yields, or substitutions were added.

sources.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, Labelling requirements for fats and oils
sources.locator: Common name: single-source and multi-source vegetable oils; olive-oil extra-virgin designation.
sources.supports: Single-source oils use source-specific common names; vegetable oil can describe multisource products and may appear in some ingredient lists. Extra virgin is a designation for olive oil. This does not identify a recipe author’s intended oil or support substitutions.

sources.title: Office québécois de la langue française, huile d’olive vierge extra (GDT)
sources.locator: Preferred term and English translation.
sources.supports: Supports huile d’olive vierge extra / extra virgin olive oil. Its displayed technical definition cites a historical 1983 source; no threshold is copied into the catalog.

decisions.reason: Add extra-virgin olive oil / huile d’olive vierge extra as a grade-qualified identity distinct from unqualified olive oil. Relink only the two recipe lines that explicitly name extra-virgin oil; do not store grade thresholds.

sources.title: Les Moulins de Soulanges, Faba Bean Flour
sources.locator: Product title, Québec mill address, and food/baking applications.
sources.supports: Supports the exact English product name and a source-named food ingredient. It does not identify a Latin name, cultivar, seed declaration, milling process, household measure, or replacement ratio.

sources.title: Les Moulins de Soulanges, Farine de Féverole
sources.locator: French product title and food/baking applications.
sources.supports: Supports the exact Québec French product title paired with the mill's English Faba Bean Flour page. It does not state a Latin name, cultivar, or process specification.

sources.title: Office québécois de la langue française, féverole (GDT)
sources.locator: Preferred French terms, Latin identification Vicia faba minor, and English plant terms.
sources.supports: Supports the French term féverole and its lexical/botanical scope Vicia faba minor. The entry names a plant and does not itself name a flour product.

sources.title: Office québécois de la langue française, gourgane (GDT)
sources.locator: Preferred Québec/Canada plant term and Latin identification Vicia faba.
sources.supports: Supports gourgane as the preferred Québec/Canada term associated with Vicia faba, which is broader than the féverole entry. It does not name a flour product.

sources.title: Province of Manitoba Agriculture, The Manitoba Advantage in Fava Beans
sources.locator: Opening paragraph: fava/faba crop names and products marketed for human consumption.
sources.supports: States fava and faba are among names for faba beans and that fava beans are marketed as flour for human food. This broad usage supports a whole-bean alias but does not establish that all faba/fava flour products share one identity.

sources.title: Cuisine Soleil, Créez votre farine
sources.locator: Cuisine Soleil gourgane-flour product amount: 1/4 cup (30 g).
sources.supports: The portion statement is specific to the separate Cuisine Soleil gourgane-flour product and is not transferable to the proposed féverole-flour identity.

decisions.reason: Add the source-named faba bean flour / farine de féverole product from Les Moulins de Soulanges as a distinct flour identity. Keep it separate from fava bean flour / farine de gourgane; the source pair and Québec terminology support this named product but not a universal botanical, process, or equivalence rule for every faba/fava flour. Add no aliases, forms, reusable measures, density, unit mappings, conversions, yields, recipe links, or substitutions. The 1/4 cup (30 g) observation belongs only to Cuisine Soleil gourgane flour.

sources.locator: Preferred term and English translation.
sources.supports: Gives mélasse de fantaisie as the preferred Québec French term and fancy molasses as its English equivalent; terminology evidence, not a product-composition standard.

sources.locator: Page 2, bilingual Crosby fancy molasses package image and label serving.
sources.supports: A historical manufacturer package image reports one tablespoon (20 g) for Crosby Fancy Molasses. Retain as a brand-specific label observation only, not a general density or cross-brand measure.

measurementObservations.foodDescription: Crosby Fancy Molasses, manufacturer package serving shown in the Pure Sweetness ebook.
measurementObservations.foodState: One brand-specific packaged fancy molasses product.
measurementObservations.measurementMethod: The manufacturer package image reports 1 tablespoon (20 g).

substitutionFindings.context: Whether cooking molasses can replace fancy molasses across brands and recipe contexts.
substitutionFindings.basis: Crosby says its own Cooking Molasses blend can commonly replace its Fancy Molasses in many recipes, with a more robust result. The statement is qualitative and supplies no ratio or defined recipe/method scope.
limitations: Keep the statement within the Crosby product family; do not generalize it to other brands or all cooking molasses.
Do not create a runtime rule or infer a reverse substitution.
The bundled recipe corpus has no molasses recipe line to provide additional context.

decisions.reason: Add the distinct Canadian fancy-molasses class as fancy molasses / mélasse de fantaisie, using OQLF for the French display, the CFIA standard for class identity, and Québec retailer wording for its qualified aliases. Keep generic molasses unresolved and preserve blackstrap, golden syrup, pomegranate molasses, and cooking-blend boundaries. Record the Crosby 1 tablespoon (20 g) label observation and qualitative Crosby cooking-blend advice only as source-specific evidence. Add no form, default density, unit mapping, conversion, recipe link, package yield, or active substitution.

sources.title: OQLF, farfalle

decisions.reason: Accept farfalle as a shape-specific pasta identity with OQLF-supported French plural farfalles and the narrower English alias bow tie pasta. Although OQLF also lists bow tie, butterfly, boucle, and papillon, keep those broad common terms out of stored aliases as a conservative catalog judgment to reduce false matches. Assign the project’s existing GRAIN_AND_CEREAL category for pasta shapes without asserting a specific grain composition. Add no forms, numeric values, conversions, yields, or substitutions.

decisions.reason: OQLF accepts farro as a term for emmer, but TERMIUM also documents farro as an ethnobotanical umbrella for einkorn, emmer, and spelt, and procurement wording does not settle recipe context. Keep farro off the emmer-wheat and emmer-flour aliases; use it only when the source or recipe context identifies the intended species/product.

Keep unqualified farro off emmer grain/flour, spelt, and einkorn identities. OQLF supports an emmer sense, while TERMIUM and the federal food-quality reference document a broader three-species use; current Canadian and Québec products use farro for both grain and flour contexts. Do not create a generic grain/flour identity or relink recipes until the product and species are specified.

The Canadian product-label recheck confirms that particular farro-labeled products are emmer grain/berries or emmer flour only when their own species and product state are explicit. OQLF gives a Québec emmer sense, while TERMIUM documents broader einkorn/emmer/spelt usage and current Metro Québec retail applies farro to pearled spelt. Keep unqualified farro unresolved and off emmer, spelt, and einkorn aliases; do not create a generic grain/flour reference. The mill baking suggestions are product-specific and do not support an active generic substitution. No active catalog, recipe, form, measurement, conversion, yield, or substitution data is added.

A current Canadian retail recheck adds another documented broad use of farro for emmer and spelt, while OQLF supports an emmer sense and Québec retail also names a pearled-spelt product farro. The evidence still does not support a single generic species or grain/flour product identity. Keep the candidate unresolved and do not add an alias, form, recipe link, or numeric behavior.

decisions.reason: Accept farro flour / farine de farro as an identity-only, species-neutral market product class. Canadian and Québec product sources use farro wording for emmer and spelt flour contexts; the producer and certificate evidence also use farro flour for einkorn and a three-species blend. The row represents only products sold or described as farro flour, not all flour made from those species. Keep the OQLF emmer sense and the distinct emmer, spelt, and einkorn identities intact. Do not add aliases, forms, density, unit mappings, measurements, conversions, yields, recipe links, or substitutions. The existing ingredient-ref-farro candidate remains unresolved for bare farro, and the R147 farro-grain identity remains a separate product class.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only fava bean flour / farine de gourgane using the manufacturer’s Québec product wording and OQLF’s preferred Québec plant name. The 30 g per 1/4 cup statement belongs to the Cuisine Soleil product only; add no aliases, forms, density, unit mapping, recipe links, conversions, yields, or substitutions.

decisions.reason: Accept finger millet / éleusine cultivée as the edible cereal grain of Eleusine coracana subsp. coracana, with ragi as its only alias. Health Canada supports the cereal subgroup, taxon, and Canadian French crop name; FAO supports the human-food grain identity and ragi. Espace pour la vie supports local French usage and grain harvest. Omit millet africain because it is also mapped to pearl millet, and omit bare millet/millet because the catalog already has a generic millet identity. Keep other Eleusine taxa, forage, feed, planting seed, flour, malt and beer products, and other processed forms outside the identity. Assign GRAIN_AND_CEREAL; add no French aliases, density, unit mappings, forms, yields, conversions, substitutions, or recipe links.

Add only kurakkan as an English alias on the existing finger-millet grain identity. Retain ragi and the Québec French display éleusine cultivée; keep kurakkan flour on the flour identity and add no other regional grain aliases, forms, numeric behavior, recipe links, or substitutions.

Add only mandua as an English alias on the existing finger-millet grain identity. Retain finger millet / éleusine cultivée, ragi, and kurakkan. Himachal Pradesh Agriculture and the Government of India's Department of Science and Technology identify Mandua as a regional name for the grain. Keep flour-qualified phrases, spelling variants, French aliases, forms, measures, recipe links, conversions, yields, and substitutions out of this grain row.

Add only ragulu as an English-search alias on the existing finger-millet grain identity. The Indian Institute of Millets Research lists Ragulu as a Telugu name for Eleusine coracana. Retain the existing French display and other aliases; add no flour-qualified spelling, form, measure, recipe link, conversion, yield, or substitution.

Add only nachni as a search alias on the existing finger-millet grain identity. FSSAI's official millet guidance lists Nachni as a Marathi name under Finger Millet (Ragi), and Mithila Foods' first-party whole-grain product page calls whole finger millet also known as Nachni. Keep the existing bilingual display and aliases; leave the qualified nachni flour alias on the separate flour reference. Add no French alias, form, measurement, recipe link, density, unit mapping, conversion, yield, or substitution.
