sources.supports: Distinguishes GMS from natural glutamate and identifies soy sauce, autolysed yeast extracts, and hydrolyzed plant proteins as other sources. Supports the same boundary in French, not a synonym or substitution.

sources.title: Lee Kum Kee Professional Canada, Premium Bouillon Powder Flavoured with Chicken
sources.locator: Product title and ingredient declaration.
sources.supports: The English Canadian manufacturer page names a chicken bouillon powder and lists yeast extract among several product-specific components. Supports the component-versus-blend boundary only.

sources.title: Lee Kum Kee Professionnel Canada, Bouillon de poulet en poudre
sources.locator: French product title and ingredient declaration.
sources.supports: The French Canadian product page also lists extrait de levure, but its full ingredient declaration differs from the English page, including its monosodium-glutamate statement. It is an independent page example, not proof of an identical SKU or formula.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only yeast extract / extrait de levure with no aliases. Canadian government material recognizes yeast extract as a food ingredient, and current ingredient suppliers list distinct commercial presentations. Keep process-qualified autolysed yeast extract, inactive nutritional yeast, baker’s yeast, MSG and other glutamate sources, bouillon blends, and Marmite/Vegemite-type spreads separate. The spread candidate remains held; its product-specific Yeast Extract / Extrait de levure retail wording is not generalized as a spread alias. No bundled recipe ingredient line requests yeast extract. Add no form, density, unit mapping, package yield, conversion, or substitution.

sources.title: Canadian Food Inspection Agency, Fish List search: Yellow Bullhead
sources.locator: Result 164041, Ameiurus natalis, common-name and family columns.
sources.supports: Lists A. natalis as Yellow Bullhead / Pimélode des marais and also lists Yellow Catfish / Silure Jaune and Bullhead / Barbotte Jaune. Nearby A. nebulosus is listed as Brown Bullhead / Barbotte and separately as Bullhead. The Fish List supports a Canadian market-name boundary, not current Québec inventory.

sources.title: Government of Canada, Quebec Fishery Regulations, Schedule 3
sources.locator: Schedule 3, Bullhead group, item (c).

sources.title: Gouvernement du Québec, Poissons d’eau douce du Québec identification poster

sources.supports: Scopes Québec barbotte in the edible-fish context to brown bullhead, A. nebulosus, and says barbotte brune was not retained for Québec fish-product labeling. Does not provide a yellow-bullhead term; supports keeping the existing barbotte reference separate.

sources.title: Gouvernement du Québec / MAPAQ, Portrait de la pêche commerciale

sources.supports: The current Québec commercial-fishing portrait identifies brown bullhead among commercial freshwater examples and principal species, without naming yellow bullhead. This is a bounded evidence gap, not proof that yellow bullhead cannot be sold.

sources.title: Gouvernement du Québec, Barbotte brune species profile

sources.supports: Identifies A. nebulosus and describes yellow bullhead / barbotte jaune as a separate similar species. Brown-bullhead commercial exploitation is not transferred to A. natalis.

substitutionFindings.context: General replacement of yellow bullhead as a fish ingredient in home cooking.
substitutionFindings.basis: The reviewed sources establish species-specific naming and distinguish yellow bullhead from brown bullhead and channel catfish, but supply no tested, quantity-backed fish replacement relationship; the bundled recipe corpus has no matching ingredient row.
limitations: Do not infer equivalent preparation, edible yield, or recipe behavior from shared bullhead or catfish wording.
Keep brown bullhead, channel catfish, and stonecat as separate species.
A future contextual rule would require a named dish, ingredient role, method, and tested quantity ratio.

decisions.reason: Add identity-only yellow bullhead / barbotte jaune for Ameiurus natalis in PROTEIN, with both alias arrays empty. The Québec fishery regulation and Québec identification poster establish the qualified bilingual species pair, and CFIA establishes Canadian label-name context. Keep the names yellow catfish, Pimélode des marais, silure jaune, bare bullhead, bare barbotte, catfish, and scientific names out of aliases. Preserve brown bullhead and channel catfish separately; add no forms, measures, mappings, recipe links, yields, conversions, or active substitutions.

Keep this seed identity separate from yellow prepared mustard, generic mustard powder, and unspecified mustard seeds.

The reviewed evidence does not establish a reusable household measure, density, mapping, or yield for this mustard-seed type. Agricultural figures, source package amounts, and branded serving information are not transferred into active recipe behavior.

sources.supports: Fixed bakery formulations use precooked yellow pea flour at 5% and 30% baker's percentage, respectively, with specified flour bases, other ingredients, and processes. These formulas do not establish a reusable substitution percentage for ordinary yellow pea flour.

sources.title: USA Dry Pea & Lentil Council and American Pulse Association, Baking with Pulse Flours for Flavor and Functionality

sources.supports: The guide presents one part yellow pea flour, one part tapioca starch, and one part white rice flour as a combined 1:1 replacement for traditional gluten flours in gluten-free baking. The 1:1 statement applies to the combined blend, not to yellow pea flour alone.

sources.title: Kotsiou et al., Impact of Roasted Yellow Split Pea Flour on Dough Rheology and Quality of Fortified Wheat Breads
sources.locator: Abstract, methods, results, and conclusions on raw and roasted yellow split-pea flour in wheat bread.
sources.supports: The study tests raw and roasted yellow split-pea flour at 10%, 15%, and 20% flour-basis replacement in specified wheat-bread formulations, with level- and process-dependent dough and bread outcomes. It does not establish a general kitchen ratio for yellow pea flour across product forms or recipe roles.

decisions.reason: Accept as the color-qualified flour made from mature dried yellow peas. Keep generic pea flour, split/green pea flour, pea protein, forms, aliases, measurements, conversions, recipe links, and substitutions outside this row.

Record Cuisine Soleil's 1/4 cup (30 g) yellow-pea-flour portion as a manufacturer-specific published observation. Do not derive a bulk density, normalize to another volume, or use the recipe book's volume-only flour amount as a mass. Keep density and unit mappings empty.

The reviewed manufacturer blend advice, fixed industry formulas, combined gluten-free blend, and controlled wheat-bread trials do not support a reusable direct substitution rule for the unqualified yellow pea flour identity. Keep the finding evidence-only with no replacements or active rule.

measurementObservations.foodDescription: Cuisine Soleil yellow pea flour, as described in its flour-blend guidance.
measurementObservations.measurementMethod: The manufacturer page states 7 g protein per 1/4 cup (30 g) of yellow pea flour; no scoop or filling method is stated.
measurementObservations.quantityBasis: Manufacturer-specific published portion only; not a reusable volume-to-mass conversion or bulk density.

substitutionFindings.context: Whether unqualified yellow pea flour has a transferable direct replacement amount for other flour ingredients across recipe roles.
substitutionFindings.basis: Cuisine Soleil recommends a three-component flour mix; the USA Dry Pea & Lentil Council and American Pulse Association describe a combined three-part gluten-free replacement blend; the pulse-industry baking formulas use precooked yellow pea flour in specified products; and the wheat-bread study tests defined raw and roasted split-pea flour levels. None establishes a standalone replacement ratio for generic yellow pea flour.
limitations: Do not encode a direct yellow-pea-flour-to-wheat-flour substitution from the combined blend guidance or the fixed precooked-flour formulas.
The controlled wheat-bread results apply only to the tested flour basis, bread formulas, and raw or roasted split-pea flour treatments.
Do not infer a universal substitution for cakes, cookies, sauces, or other recipe roles.

sources.title: Argentina, Código Alimentario Argentino, Capítulo XV, Productos estimulantes o fruitivos

decisions.reason: Add yerba mate elaborada / yerba mate elaborada as a distinct HERB identity for the source-defined dry processed leaf product.
